differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Loki indexes metadata (labels) of logs, not full text, enabling efficient querying and lower storage costs by indexing only label dimensions.
differences.rightDesc: Elasticsearch indexes log content and metadata into documents, offering powerful full-text search and complex aggregations but with higher indexing overhead.

differences.title: 2. INDEXING STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: Loki's index is small, containing only label sets, making it fast to query and economical. Log content is retrieved directly from object storage.
differences.rightDesc: Elasticsearch builds inverted indexes for all searchable fields, enabling rapid searches across vast amounts of text data at the cost of storage and CPU.

differences.title: 3. STORAGE ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Loki stores compressed log content in object storage (S3, GCS), leveraging its scalability and cost-effectiveness. Index is separate.
differences.rightDesc: Elasticsearch stores indexed data across a cluster of nodes, managing replication and sharding for high availability and search performance.

differences.title: 4. QUERY LANGUAGE
differences.leftDesc: LogQL is designed for log patterns, label filtering, and metric generation from logs. It's simpler and optimized for log data.
differences.rightDesc: ES Query DSL is a powerful, JSON-based language for complex searches, aggregations, and analytical queries across diverse data types.

differences.title: 5. OPERATIONAL COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Loki's architecture with decoupled index and object storage often leads to simpler deployments and maintenance, especially for log-specific use cases.
differences.rightDesc: Elasticsearch requires careful cluster tuning, shard management, and monitoring for optimal performance and stability, especially at scale.

differences.title: 6. COST EFFICIENCY
differences.leftDesc: Loki's approach minimizes indexing overhead and leverages cheap object storage, making it highly cost-efficient for ingesting and retaining large volumes of logs.
differences.rightDesc: Elasticsearch's extensive indexing and distributed nature can lead to higher infrastructure and operational costs, especially for long-term log retention.

differences.title: 7. PRIMARY USE CASE
differences.leftDesc: Loki excels at collecting, querying, and analyzing logs, integrating seamlessly with Prometheus and Grafana for unified observability.
differences.rightDesc: Elasticsearch is a general-purpose search engine ideal for log analysis, full-text search, APM, security analytics, and business intelligence.
